description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics — Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy (change in accuracy), and Initial Accuracy — for a large language model’s response to external feedback. The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” spans from 0.95 to 0.99 on a linear scale, with tick marks at 0.95, 0.96, 0.97, and 0.99; a gray rectangular region is shaded between approximately 0.975 and 0.985. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, with major gridlines at intervals of 0.2. The “Final Acc” line (solid blue with circle markers) starts at approximately 0.88 at 0.95 initial confidence, rises slightly to a peak of ~0.91 at 0.98, then declines to ~0.87 at 0.99. The “Δ Acc” line (dashed orange with diamond markers) begins at ~0.89 at 0.95, remains relatively flat until 0.98 (~0.87), then drops sharply to ~0.75 at 0.99. The “Initial Acc” line (dashed green with square markers) remains near zero across the entire range, rising slightly from 0.0 at 0.95 to ~0.12 at 0.99, indicating minimal initial accuracy regardless of confidence level. Error bars are present on all data points, showing variability in measurements.
